chapter: Los Angeles scene in the 1930s and 40s
title: The Lincoln Theater stage shows and Harry Levette
summary: She recalls the Lincoln Theater's stage shows produced by Bardu Ali and local talent nights run by Harry Levette in 1947.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: When you mentioned -- we were talking
What year would that have been?
That must have been -- well, it had to be in '47, because that's when I started recording, you see, and it was just before -- oh, it was just before I went east.
And the Lincoln Theater is on Central Avenue between 22nd and 23rd?
Adams. Somewhere around there, yes. Around Adams, uh-huh. I think now -- I think it's owned by some religious group now, if I'm not mistaken. It's a church or something now.
But in the '40s, and I guess before the '40s, it was the main theater in the Central Avenue area, wasn't it?

Stage shows. Marvelous stage shows. I can remember Bard u Ali , who's out here, and Pigmeat Markham. They came out here from New York, you know. Bard u's still here. And they -- he used to sort of produce the shows at the Lincoln Theater. And there was another man,

Harry Levett, who's passed on. Harry Levett used to show the -- exhibit the local talent, any local talent that he'd think had possibilities, you know. He was very good, and he also wrote for the -- I think he wrote for the Sentinel for a little while, the Sentinel, the Los Angeles Sentinel, and he probably before that wrote for the Eagle, the Los Angeles Eagle. That was a black paper also. He wrote for those papers. But he was very good at staging shows and trying to show the local talent off.
Was that some kind of an arrangement where it would be like once a week with the local talent, or was it a full week show presenting local talent?
Like once a week. I think we did it once a week. Might hve been -- might have been two days, but I know it wasn't more than that, you know. At the Lincoln Theater.
And that would be, say, once a week, and the rest of the week would be what? Out of town?
Movies or -- no, the rest of the week would be just movies, you know, most likely. But on the weekends they would have shows.
There wasn't ever a period when there was live entertainment every day?
Yes, sometimes there would be. Yes, sometimes where would be. It depended, you know, on who. Now,
as I say, I think when Bardu Ali was there I think they used to have stage shows every night. The shows would run for maybe a week or two, you know, at a time.
